requirements.subject: ent:user-defined-type
requirements.canonical: A user-defined type SHALL be denoted by the keyword `type`.
requirements.original: User-defined types shall be denoted by the keyword type.

requirements.subject: ent:user-defined-type
requirements.canonical: A user-defined type MAY define a subtype (such as a list, range or length restriction) of a basic type, a structured type or the `anytype` according to table 3.
requirements.original: With user-defined types it is possible to create subtypes (such as lists, ranges and length restrictions) on basic types, structured types and anytype according to table 3.

requirements.subject: ent:subtype
requirements.canonical: A value of a subtype SHALL fulfil the conditions specified by the constraint of the subtype.
requirements.original: Values of a subtype shall fulfil conditions specified by its constraint and all constraints existing in all its direct and indirect parent types up to the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:subtype
requirements.canonical: A value of a subtype SHALL fulfil all constraints of all direct and indirect parent types of the subtype up to the core type.
requirements.original: Values of a subtype shall fulfil conditions specified by its constraint and all constraints existing in all its direct and indirect parent types up to the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:template-list-constraint
requirements.canonical: A subtype definition MAY specify a list of distinguished templates as subtype constraint, as listed in table 3.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 permits the specification of a list of distinguished templates as listed in table 3.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: Each template in a template list constraint SHALL be an instance of the type being constrained.
requirements.original: The templates in the list shall be instances of the type being constrained and the set of values matching at least one of these templates shall be a subset of the values defined by the type being constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:template-list-constraint
requirements.canonical: The set of values matching at least one template of a template list constraint SHALL be a subset of the values defined by the type being constrained.
requirements.original: The templates in the list shall be instances of the type being constrained and the set of values matching at least one of these templates shall be a subset of the values defined by the type being constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:template-list-constraint
requirements.canonical: A subtype defined by a template list constraint restricts its allowed values to the values matching at least one of the templates in the list.
requirements.original: The subtype defined by this list restricts the allowed values of the subtype to those values matching at least one of the templates in the list.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template in a template list constraint SHALL only reference (directly or indirectly) other templates or constant expressions.
requirements.original: The templates in the list shall only (directly or indirectly) reference other templates or constant expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:constant-expression
requirements.canonical: A constant expression used (directly or indirectly) in a template of a template list constraint SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10 for constant expressions used in type definitions.
requirements.original: Constant expressions used (directly or indirectly) in the template expressions shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10 for constant expressions used in type definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:type-list-constraint
requirements.canonical: A subtype definition MAY specify a list of subtypes as subtype constraint, as listed in table 3.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 permits the specification of a list of subtypes as listed in table 3 for value lists.

requirements.subject: ent:type-list-constraint
requirements.canonical: Each type in a type list constraint SHALL be a subtype of the root type of the type being defined.
requirements.original: The types in the list shall be subtypes of the root type.

requirements.subject: ent:type-list-constraint
requirements.canonical: A subtype defined by a type list constraint restricts its allowed values to the union of the values of the referenced subtypes.
requirements.original: The subtype defined by this list restricts the allowed values of the subtype to the union of the values of the referenced subtypes.

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.canonical: A range constraint MAY be specified for the types `integer`, `charstring`, `universal charstring` and `float` and for types derived from them.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 permits the specification of range constraints for the types integer, charstring, `universal` charstring and float (or derivations of these types).

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.condition: the range constraint is applied to integer or float
requirements.canonical: For `integer` and `float`, a subtype defined by a range constraint restricts its allowed values to the values in the range, including or excluding the lower boundary and/or the upper boundary.
requirements.original: For integer and float, the subtype defined by the range restricts the allowed values of the subtype to the values in the range including or excluding the lower boundary and/or the upper boundary.

requirements.subject: ent:range-boundary
requirements.canonical: For `integer` and `float` range constraints, each range boundary MAY be inclusive or exclusive.
requirements.original: For integer and float, the subtype defined by the range restricts the allowed values of the subtype to the values in the range including or excluding the lower boundary and/or the upper boundary.

requirements.subject: ent:range-boundary
requirements.canonical: The upper boundary of a range constraint SHALL be greater than or equal to the lower boundary.
requirements.original: The upper boundary shall be greater than or equal to the lower boundary.

requirements.subject: ent:infinity-keyword
requirements.canonical: In an integer range constraint, `-infinity` MAY be used instead of a lower boundary value and `infinity` instead of an upper boundary value to indicate that there is no lower or upper boundary.
requirements.original: In order to specify an infinite integer range, the keyword -infinity or infinity can be used instead of a value indicating that there is no lower or upper boundary; -infinity shall not be used as the upper bound and infinity shall not be used as the lower bound for integer ranges.

ambiguity.issue: '-infinity' is called a keyword although only 'infinity' is a keyword; '-infinity' is the negated keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:infinity-keyword
requirements.canonical: `-infinity` SHALL NOT be used as the upper boundary of an integer range constraint.
requirements.original: In order to specify an infinite integer range, the keyword -infinity or infinity can be used instead of a value indicating that there is no lower or upper boundary; -infinity shall not be used as the upper bound and infinity shall not be used as the lower bound for integer ranges.

requirements.subject: ent:infinity-keyword
requirements.canonical: `infinity` SHALL NOT be used as the lower boundary of an integer range constraint.
requirements.original: In order to specify an infinite integer range, the keyword -infinity or infinity can be used instead of a value indicating that there is no lower or upper boundary; -infinity shall not be used as the upper bound and infinity shall not be used as the lower bound for integer ranges.

requirements.subject: ent:infinity-keyword
requirements.canonical: In a `float` range constraint, `-infinity` or `infinity` MAY be used as the boundaries.
requirements.original: Also for float, -infinity or infinity can be used as the bounds in range restrictions.

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.canonical: A `float` range constraint with `-infinity` as lower boundary does not restrict the allowed numerical values downward and includes the special value `-infinity`.
requirements.original: Using the special value -infinity as the lower bound shall indicate that the allowed numerical values are not restricted downward and the special value -infinity is also included.

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.canonical: A `float` range constraint whose lower and upper boundaries both denote `-infinity` includes no numerical values and only the special value `-infinity`.
requirements.original: If both the lower and upper bounds denote -infinity, no numerical values are included, only the special value -infinity.

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.canonical: A `float` range constraint with `infinity` as upper boundary does not restrict the allowed numerical values upward and includes the special value `infinity`.
requirements.original: Using the special value infinity as the upper bound shall indicate that the allowed numerical values are not restricted upward and the special value infinity is also included.

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.canonical: A `float` range constraint whose lower and upper boundaries both denote `infinity` includes no numerical values and only the special value `infinity`.
requirements.original: If both the lower and upper bounds denote infinity, no numerical values are included, only the special value infinity.

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.condition: an exclusive infinity bound is used
requirements.canonical: A `float` range constraint with an exclusive boundary `!-infinity` or `!infinity` includes the respective unrestricted numerical float values but not the special value `-infinity` or `infinity`.
requirements.original: If exclusive bounds (!infinity or !-infinity) is used instead, only the respective numerical float values are included in the range.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether 'instead' refers to the general case of an infinity bound or only to the preceding case where both bounds denote the same infinity; the general reading was chosen.
readings: A float range constraint with an exclusive boundary !-infinity or !infinity includes the unrestricted numerical float values but not the special value -infinity or infinity.
A float range constraint whose both boundaries are exclusive (!-infinity .. !-infinity or !infinity .. !infinity) includes only numerical float values, i.e. it is empty.

requirements.subject: ent:not-a-number-keyword
requirements.canonical: The special value `not_a_number` SHALL NOT be used in a `float` range constraint.
requirements.original: In case of float, the special value not_a_number is not allowed in a range constraint.

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.condition: the range constraint is applied to charstring or universal charstring
requirements.canonical: For `charstring` and `universal charstring` types, a range constraint restricts the allowed values of each separate character in the strings.
requirements.original: In the case of charstring and universal charstring types, the range restricts the allowed values for each separate character in the strings.

requirements.subject: ent:range-boundary
requirements.canonical: The boundaries of a character string range constraint SHALL evaluate to valid (non-empty) character positions according to the coded character set table(s) of the type.
requirements.original: The boundaries shall evaluate to valid character positions according to the coded character set table(s) of the type (e.g. the given position shall not be empty).

requirements.subject: ent:range-constraint
requirements.canonical: An empty position of the coded character set table between the lower and the upper boundaries of a character string range constraint is not a valid value of the range.
requirements.original: Empty positions between the lower and the upper boundaries are not considered to be valid values of the specified range.

requirements.subject: ent:constant-expression
requirements.canonical: A constant used in a constant expression defining a range boundary SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions defining the values shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.
